clue.text: Waiter, don't just stand there !

parts.note: an order to a restaurant attendant to stop idling and bring the food, echoing Milton's line about those who only stand and wait

explanation.walkthrough: Milton wrote 'They also serve who only stand and wait'; the clue tells the waiter that standing is not enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A waiter's job is to bring food to diners, which is what he is urged to do instead of standing idle.

clue.text: Food for circus-goers?

parts.note: a circus is a show, so its audience might eat 'show' bread

explanation.walkthrough: The biblical loaves set out in the Temple were spelt with the old form 'shew' of 'show', and a circus is a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The consecrated loaves displayed in the Jewish Temple, read playfully as bread for people going to a show.

clue.text: The problem of Paul Revere for instance?

explanation.walkthrough: Paul Revere galloped through Massachusetts in 1775 to warn that the British were coming.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a supplementary exercise following a theorem is so called; Revere famously made a midnight journey on horseback.

clue.text: Tear in pieces a bird made of clay

indicators.note: torn into bits, so the letters of the word before are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: a hen is a farmyard bird

explanation.surface: A violent act of ripping apart a clay bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' looks like weeping or ripping, but 'in pieces' tells you to shuffle its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthenware pottery is fired clay, so the adjective describes things fashioned from that material.

clue.text: Friar's dances frequented by Bunter

parts.note: Friar Tuck of the Robin Hood legends, with the possessive S
hops are informal dances

explanation.surface: A merry monk's jigs that a fat schoolboy likes to attend.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is the greedy schoolboy of Frank Richards's Greyfriars stories, forever haunting the school snack shop; British schools' shops selling sweets and cakes are so named.
explanation.definitionFit: School snack counters are the places that gluttonous fictional schoolboy constantly visited.

clue.text: Notwithstanding that mother's boy is a saint

parts.note: 'tho' is a short spelling of though, meaning notwithstanding that
Ma is mother, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: Despite being a mummy's boy, someone is declared holy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boy is' links the pieces to the definition; the name is a common boy's name as well as the apostle's.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle known as Doubting Thomas is a canonised saint.

clue.text: Scheme to place a hundred on a Salisbury landmark

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written
Salisbury Cathedral's tall steeple is the city's famous landmark

explanation.surface: A plan to bet a hundred pounds involving a famous cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: Salisbury Cathedral in Wiltshire has the tallest church steeple in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To plot secretly with others is to scheme, used here as a verb.

clue.text: It may be full of motes and get in your eye too

definitions.text: It may be full of motes and get in your eye too

parts.words: It may be full of motes and get in your eye too
parts.note: a shaft of light shows dust specks and can dazzle, while the Gospel speaks of the mote and the beam in the eye

explanation.walkthrough: Matthew 7 contrasts the mote in your brother's eye with the beam in your own; a ray of sunlight shows floating dust.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray of daylight reveals dancing dust particles and can shine straight into a person's eyes.

clue.text: Work is urgent, gets us down

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
something that presses demands immediate attention

explanation.surface: Pressing tasks at the office leave everyone depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh heavily on people, making them low, is to burden or crush them.

clue.text: Yugoslav dichotomy

explanation.walkthrough: The city is on the Dalmatian coast, part of Yugoslavia when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: A port city on the Croatian coast, formerly in Yugoslavia, shares its name with a division into two.

clue.text: Princess not up, we hear? Still under this!

indicators.note: the clue tells us to listen to how the phrase is spoken

parts.note: Princess Ida is the heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera; down means not up

explanation.surface: Someone is told the princess has not yet risen and is still in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ida down' spoken sounds like the name of a quilt stuffed with duck feathers; someone not up is still lying under it.
explanation.definitionFit: A late riser is still beneath the warm feather quilt on the bed.

clue.text: The French writer returns to the country

indicators.note: turns back, so the two pieces before are read backwards as one run

parts.note: la is French for 'the'
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A French author goes back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns LAPEN into the Himalayan kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A Himalayan kingdom between India and Tibet is a sovereign state.

clue.text: Annual tribute

parts.note: a gift offered once a year on the anniversary of someone's arrival in the world

explanation.definitionFit: A gift given every year on someone's anniversary of being born is a yearly offering.

clue.text: Some of the rarer minerals are found in this street

indicators.note: only part of the following words is wanted, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Unusual rocks turn up along a certain road.
explanation.walkthrough: Ermine Street was a Roman road from London to Lincoln and York.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman road running north from London bears that name, also that of a stoat's white winter fur.

clue.text: Poor beggar says he's ineligible for the Reform Club

definitions.text: Poor beggar says he's ineligible for the Reform Club

parts.words: Poor beggar says he's ineligible for the Reform Club
parts.note: a pauper who cannot reform himself says '...', and the Reform Club is a London gentlemen's club

explanation.walkthrough: Reform means mend; split as MEND I CANT, the word is the beggar admitting he cannot mend his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living by begging is a pauper.

clue.text: When introduced, simpered in embarrassment

indicators.note: flustered and confused, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone smirked shyly on being introduced to a stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in embarrassment' rearranges SIMPERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stated beforehand as a basis for argument has been laid down as a starting assumption.

clue.text: Muck-spreading at the crossroads ?

parts.note: spreading manure is filthy labour, recalling the old melodrama phrase about villainy at the crossroads

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty work at the crossroads' is a stock phrase from Victorian melodrama for skulduggery.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading manure is literally filthy labour, and the phrase also means underhand villainy.

clue.text: Not one of the upper crust schools ?

definitions.text: Not one of the upper crust schools ?

parts.words: Not one of the upper crust schools
parts.note: a school that is the opposite of upper might be on the lower side

explanation.walkthrough: Downside is a Catholic boarding school in Somerset; its name read as 'down side' is the opposite of upper.
explanation.definitionFit: A Somerset public school whose name suggests the lower side, contrary to the upper crust.

clue.text: Corban

parts.note: a biblical word for an offering dedicated to God

explanation.definitionFit: Corban, in the Gospel of Mark, is a gift vowed to God, i.e. a contribution.

clue.text: Cassava pudding

explanation.definitionFit: The starch made from the cassava root is used to make a milk dessert of the same name.

clue.text: One who maltreats a vehicle when about to reverse

parts.note: a bus is a road vehicle

indicators.note: the word for about is turned round

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A reckless driver backs a bus about carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reverse' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who treats others badly or cruelly is a mistreater.

clue.text: "Gaily A gallant knight " sought Eldorado

parts.note: the missing word from the opening of Poe's poem Eldorado, which begins 'Gaily ___, A gallant knight'

explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap in Poe's lines 'Gaily bedight, / A gallant knight, / In sunshine and in shadow'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word meaning adorned, which completes the first line of Poe's poem Eldorado.

clue.text: She helps to keep Topsy cheerful

indicators.note: the following words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A woman assists in keeping a child happy.
explanation.walkthrough: Topsy is the slave girl in Uncle Tom's Cabin; Psyche is the mortal girl loved by Cupid.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the soul personified is a girl beloved of Eros, so a female figure.

clue.text: Making a golf shot on to the turf, somewhere in Lancs or Glos

parts.note: chipping is playing a short lofted shot onto the green
sod is a piece of turf
Bury is a town in Lancashire, a county in north-west England

explanation.surface: A golfer lofts the ball onto the grass at a course in the north or west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Glos is Gloucestershire, a county in western England, where this market town lies; 'or' separates the Lancashire piece from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town near Bristol lies in Gloucestershire, the county abbreviated Glos.

clue.text: Measure to make two into eight, say

indicators.note: the instruction to speak the phrase so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: raising two to its third power gives eight, so one must 'cube it'

explanation.surface: An arithmetic puzzle about multiplying two to reach eight.
explanation.walkthrough: Two cubed is eight; 'cube it' said aloud is the ancient length.
explanation.definitionFit: An old unit of length based on the forearm is a measure.

clue.text: You, sir-do you hear ? — join up !

indicators.note: asks us to listen to the spoken sound of the pieces

parts.note: taken as written; a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: A sergeant bellows at a recruit to enlist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' plus KNIGHT (a man titled Sir) spoken together sound like the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To combine or come together is to merge.

clue.text: It seems to be a negative type of jollification

parts.note: be, the verb itself
no is a negative reply

explanation.surface: A party that is apparently a non-event.
explanation.walkthrough: A beano is British slang for a riotous party or spree.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a noisy celebration or spree, a festive bash.

clue.text: Can go back inside in company that's disguised

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one piece is put within the abbreviation for company
both words before are read backwards together

parts.note: a tin is a can
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tin returns inside a firm in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TINGO into OGNIT; 'Can' is a noun here, a tin, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling under a false identity means concealing who one is.

clue.text: Summit meeting ?

parts.note: a summit is a top, and heads are tops, so a meeting of heads face to face

explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase is literally 'head to head': two heads, the tops of people, meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A private two-person conversation, literally French for head to head.

clue.text: Take the Occident at a pinch ?

definitions.text: Take the Occident at a pinch ?

parts.words: Take the Occident at a pinch
parts.note: to pinch and twist something sharply between the fingers, with 'Occident' (the West) hinting at the letters of the word

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'pinch', a sharp nip with the fingers; the rest plays on the West hiding in the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp pinch or twist given with the fingers is a nip.
